chapter_title: Day 9, Part 1: Knossos, the Minoans, and Linear B
learning_objective: The learner will interpret a timeline of Knossos from its first village to the decipherment of Linear B, answering at least 3 of 4 prediction questions about the order and spacing of events correctly before each answer is revealed.
specification:
Type: timeline **sim-id:** knossos-village-to-decipherment-timeline
**Library:** vis-timeline
**Status:** Specified
**Bloom Level:** Understand
**Bloom Verb:** interpret
**Learning Objective:** The learner will interpret a timeline of Knossos from its first village to the decipherment of Linear B, answering at least 3 of 4 prediction questions about the order and spacing of events correctly before each answer is revealed. **Prerequisites:** Knossos Palace, Arthur Evans, Evans reconstructions (Part One); palace economy and the Thera eruption (Part Two); the Snake Goddess figurines, the Phaistos Disc, Linear A, Linear B, and palace scribes (Part Four); the Bronze Age collapse (Chapter 8). **Evidence of Mastery:** The learner answers four prediction questions, each locked in before the relevant events appear on the timeline. An answer is correct when it matches the Correct answer column in Content. Mastery is 3 of 4 correct. Zooming, panning, and opening event descriptions after the reveal are exploration, not evidence. **Misconceptions:** (1) The Thera eruption destroyed Minoan Crete at once. (2) Knossos and its tablets fell in the same disaster as the mainland palaces. (3) Linear B was read soon after the tablets were found. (4) The palace we see is all from one moment. **Instructional Rationale:** Prediction before reveal makes the learner commit to a mental timeline and then confront the actual spacing, which is what makes the long gaps (a century between Thera and the destruction of the palaces, 52 years between the first tablets and their decipherment) memorable. A to-scale timeline shows those gaps directly. **Content:** Two bands share one timeline: "Bronze Age Crete" and "Rediscovery." Events, all of which appear on the timeline: | # | Date | Band | Event label | Description shown on click | |---|---|---|---|---| | 1 | c. 7000 BCE | Bronze Age Crete | First village at Knossos | A farming village on the Kephala hill, one of the oldest settlements in Europe. | | 2 | c. 1900 BCE | Bronze Age Crete | First palace | The first palace is built around the central court. | | 3 | c. 1700 BCE | Bronze Age Crete | Second palace | After earthquake damage, the palace is rebuilt on a grander scale. | | 4 | c. 1700 BCE | Bronze Age Crete | Phaistos Disc | The stamped clay disc is made at Phaistos. | | 5 | c. 1600 BCE | Bronze Age Crete | Thera erupts | Akrotiri is buried; Minoan Crete is weakened but carries on. | | 6 | c. 1600 BCE | Bronze Age Crete | Snake Goddess figurines | The faience figures later found in the Temple Repositories are made. | | 7 | c. 1450 BCE | Bronze Age Crete | Mycenaeans at Knossos | Most Minoan palaces are destroyed; Greek speakers rule Knossos and write Linear B. | | 8 | c. 1375 BCE | Bronze Age Crete | Knossos burns | The palace is destroyed by fire; the fire bakes the Linear B tablets. | | 9 | c. 1200 BCE | Bronze Age Crete | Mainland palaces fall | Pylos and other palaces burn in the Bronze Age collapse; Linear B ends. | | 10 | 1878 | Rediscovery | Kalokairinos digs | Minos Kalokairinos finds the storerooms and their giant jars. | | 11 | 1900 | Rediscovery | Evans begins | Arthur Evans begins excavating; the Throne Room and the first tablets are found. | | 12 | 1903 | Rediscovery | Snake Goddesses found | Evans finds the faience figurines in the Temple Repositories. | | 13 | 1908 | Rediscovery | Phaistos Disc found | Luigi Pernier finds the disc at Phaistos. | | 14 | c. 1905–1930 | Rediscovery | Evans reconstructions | Parts of the palace are rebuilt, mainly in reinforced concrete from the 1920s. | | 15 | 1952 | Rediscovery | Linear B is read | Michael Ventris shows that Linear B writes Greek. | | 16 | 2025 | Rediscovery | UNESCO listing | The Minoan palatial centres of Crete, including Knossos, become a World Heritage Site. | Prediction questions, in this order: | # | Question (shown before the reveal) | Choices | Correct answer | Events revealed after answering | |---|---|---|---|---| | 1 | Did the Thera eruption come before or after most Minoan palaces were destroyed? | Before; At the same time; After | Before | 5 and 7 | | 2 | About how many years separate the Thera eruption and the destruction of most Minoan palaces? | About 10; About 150; About 500 | About 150 | 2, 3, 4, 6 (the rest of the Bronze Age Crete band up to event 7) | | 3 | Did Knossos burn before, at the same time as, or after the mainland palaces such as Pylos? | Before; At the same time; After | Before | 8 and 9 | | 4 | How many years passed between Evans finding the first tablets and Ventris reading them? | About 5; About 50; About 150 | About 50 | 10 to 16 | **Provenance:** All dates come from this chapter: Part One ("Knossos Palace," "Arthur Evans," "Evans Reconstructions"), Part Two ("Thera Eruption"), and Part Four ("Snake Goddess Figurines," "Phaistos Disc," "Linear B," "Palace Scribes"), and from Chapter 4's World Heritage table (2025). Bronze Age dates are approximate; the timeline labels them "c." and the sim shows the note "Bronze Age dates are approximate and debated; the destruction of Knossos is sometimes dated later than 1375 BCE." **Rules:** The timeline is to scale from 7000 BCE to 2030 CE, with a zoom control (buttons, not the mouse wheel) to expand the Bronze Age band. Question 2's answer is computed as 1600 − 1450 = 150 years. Question 4's answer is computed as 1952 − 1900 = 52 years, which rounds to "About 50." Event 1 is shown from the start so the learner sees the full scale. Events 10 to 16 and 2 to 9 stay hidden until their question is answered, as listed. After all four questions, every event is visible. **Learner Activity:** 1. The learner sees the empty two-band timeline with event 1 only, and question 1. 2. The learner answers question 1; events 5 and 7 appear, and the gap between them is labeled. 3. The learner answers questions 2 to 4 in turn; after each, the listed events appear. 4. After question 4, the learner can click any event to read its description and zoom into the Bronze Age band. 5. The learner should notice the long gap between the Bronze Age band and the Rediscovery band, and that the record keepers of Knossos were silent for more than 3,000 years before anyone read their tablets. **Feedback:** Four questions, fixed order, one attempt each. Correct: "Right." plus the reason. Incorrect: "Not quite: [correct answer]." plus the reason. Reasons: (1) "Thera erupted about 1600 BCE; most palaces fell about 1450 BCE, so the eruption weakened Crete but did not end it." (2) "1600 − 1450 = about 150 years, several generations." (3) "Knossos burned about 1375 BCE in the usual dating, more than a century before the mainland palaces fell around 1200 BCE." (4) "Evans found tablets in 1900; Ventris read them in 1952: 52 years, about 50." A score "Predictions correct: n of 4" is shown. **Starting State:** The to-scale axis from 7000 BCE to 2030 CE, event 1 visible, the two band labels, and question 1 with the prompt "Before we fill this in: what came first, the volcano or the fall?" **Chapter Anchors:** First village about 7000 BCE; first palace about 1900 BCE; rebuilt about 1700 BCE; Phaistos Disc about 1700 BCE; Thera about 1600 BCE; Snake Goddesses about 1600 BCE; Mycenaeans at Knossos after about 1450 BCE; Knossos burns about 1375 BCE; Pylos around 1200 BCE; Kalokairinos 1878; Evans 1900; Snake Goddesses found 1903; disc found 1908; reconstructions about 1905 to 1930; Linear B read 1952; UNESCO 2025.
